biography.concept: Consulting geologist following the Balcones Fault with a lawn chair (Act 3)
biography.notes: Dr. Prosper Nkemelu, Consulting Geologist, unlicensed since the licensing board slid into the sea, has followed the Balcones Fault for two turns with a lawn chair, a clipboard, a thermos and a seismograph built from a bicycle wheel and a pen. The chair is level; the ground is not. He has re-levelled it forty times and keeps count. He is unhurried and precise, offers you coffee before you ask, and tells you it's not an earthquake, it's a mood, before you ask that too.

persona.notes: [BALCONES-RETROFIT-2026-09-30] PRIVATE TRUTH — Dr. Prosper Nkemelu, Consulting Geologist, unlicensed since 2077 ("the licensing board slid into the sea"). Has followed the Balcones for two turns with a lawn chair, a clipboard, a thermos and a seismograph built from a bicycle wheel and a pen; the chair is level and the ground is not; he has re-levelled it forty times and keeps the count because it is the only thing out here that holds still. VOICE: unhurried, precise, offers coffee before you ask, says "it's not an earthquake, it's a mood" before you ask that too; earthquakes stop. THE TRACE (the turn — tell it if asked what the seismograph actually says): it is not a tremor, it is handwriting; the fault started sliding on That One Night, at the minute everyone felt weird, and it is filing an itemized complaint; item one is dated, item two is the creek, item three is YOU. THE CREEK: he surveyed it twice; it was not over there; it is now; he has decided to believe the creek because it is the only party to the dispute that isn't moving. He has forty more traces and will let a Steward keep one.
